title: No common zero and permutation invariance
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $n\ge1$. Write $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with structure morphisms $q_1,q_n$ (the first projections). Let $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n=\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\cdots\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ be the $n$-fold fibre product over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product] (formed inductively, $(\mathbf P^1_S)^1=\mathbf P^1_S$, $(\mathbf P^1_S)^m=(\mathbf P^1_S)^{m-1}\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$), with its projections $\mathrm{pr}_i:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^1_S$ ($1\le i\le n$) and $p_n=q_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_i:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to S$; a morphism $T\to(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ is the same as an $n$-tuple of morphisms $a_i:T\to\mathbf P^1_S$ with $q_1\circ a_1=\dots=q_1\circ a_n$.

*The sections.* Let $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ be the twisting sheaf of $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[T_0,T_1]$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist] (with $A=\mathbf Z$, $n=1$), with its global sections $T_0,T_1$ (on $D_+(T_k)$, $T_l=(T_l/T_k)\,e_k^{(1)}$), let $\mathcal O(1)$ on $\mathbf P^1_S$ be its pullback along the second projection $\mathbf P^1_S\to\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$, with the pulled-back sections $T_0,T_1$, and put

$$
\mathcal L_n=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathrm{pr}_n^*\mathcal O(1),\qquad x_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_0,\ \ y_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_1\in\Gamma\bigl((\mathbf P^1_S)^n,\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal O(1)\bigr),
$$

an invertible $\mathcal O_{(\mathbf P^1_S)^n}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] (the line bundle $\mathcal O(1,\dots,1)$). Let $F_0,\dots,F_n\in\mathbf Z[x_1,y_1,\dots,x_n,y_n]$ be the polynomials of [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism], $\prod_{i=1}^n(x_it+y_i)=\sum_{j=0}^nF_jt^j$. Then:

(a) $F_j=\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\},\,|J|=j}m_J$ with $m_J=\prod_{i\in J}x_i\prod_{i\notin J}y_i$; so $F_j$ is multihomogeneous of degree $(1,\dots,1)$ in the pairs $(x_i,y_i)$, and we also write $F_j$ for the global section $\sum_{|J|=j}u_{J,1}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{J,n}$ of $\mathcal L_n$, where $u_{J,i}=x_i$ for $i\in J$ and $u_{J,i}=y_i$ for $i\notin J$.

(b) (*no common zero*) For every point $z$ of $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ some $F_j(z)\ne0$ in the fibre $\mathcal L_n(z)=\mathcal L_{n,z}\otimes\kappa(z)$; that is, $F_0,\dots,F_n$ generate $\mathcal L_n$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points].

(c) Hence the *symmetric-product morphism*

$$
\sigma_n:=\varphi_{p_n,(\mathcal L_n,(F_0,\dots,F_n))}:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\longrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S
$$

of [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is defined: $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma_n=p_n$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n=\psi_{(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))}:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, the morphism with $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L_n$, $\psi^*T_j\mapsto F_j$; on coordinates it is $((x_1:y_1),\dots,(x_n:y_n))\mapsto[F_0:\cdots:F_n]$.

(d) (*$S_n$-invariance*) For a permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $\tau_\pi:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ be the morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\tau_\pi=\mathrm{pr}_{\pi(i)}$ for all $i$ (an automorphism over $S$, with inverse $\tau_{\pi^{-1}}$). Then there is an isomorphism $\beta_\pi:\tau_\pi^*\mathcal L_n\to\mathcal L_n$ with $\beta_\pi(\tau_\pi^*F_j)=F_j$ for all $j$ (the $F_j$ are $S_n$-invariant), and $\sigma_n\circ\tau_\pi=\sigma_n$.

proof.text: Expand the product using Finset.prod_add and collect the coefficient of t^j. Each product over J is the monomial whose exponent vector has one in the first coordinate for i in J and in the second coordinate for i outside J. The support of the sum is contained in the union of these singleton supports, proving multidegree (1,...,1).

proof.text: Pullback preserves invertibility of O(1); induction on the positive tensor family proves invertibility of L. Apply the coefficient-section nonvanishing theorem to the underlying scheme maps pr_i. It uses the standard coordinate cover and the unique nonzero summand in F_|J|, with J the indices where the second coordinate vanishes. Convert this nonvanishing condition into the epimorphism from the free module by the invertible-generating-sections-fibre criterion.

proof.text: Apply the universal property of the product cone in Over S to the projections reindexed by pi and pi inverse. The two lifted maps are inverse because their composites have the identity projections. Apply the coefficient-section permutation theorem to the underlying endomorphism and its projection equalities, obtaining beta and its compatibility with each F_j.

proof.text: The pullback compatibility of the projective-space functor of points supplies an isomorphism for the composite tau followed by psi. Compose it with beta. The resulting isomorphism identifies the pulled homogeneous coordinates with the original F_j, so the uniqueness clause of generatingSections_integralHom_exists proves tau followed by psi equals psi. The two morphisms tau followed by sigma and sigma have equal structure maps since tau is over S, and equal integral projections by this equality. The uniqueness clause of homOfGeneratingSections_spec proves their equality.

split_report.summary: Made the statement precise without changing sigma_n: it is now explicitly the morphism phi_{p_n,(L_n,(F_j))} of def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections (created by the over-base worker; same name, same formula, same L_n = pr_1^*O(1) (x) ... (x) pr_n^*O(1), x_i = pr_i^*T_0, y_i = pr_i^*T_1 as in lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-over-base), with O(1) on P^1_S the pullback of the twisting sheaf of P^1_Z (def-pc-projective-space-twist). Stated (a) the coefficient formula F_j = sum_{|J|=j} prod_J x_i prod_{J^c} y_i and the meaning of F_j as a section of L_n; (b) no common zero as fibrewise non-vanishing (the generation condition of lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points); (c) the definition of sigma_n; (d) S_n-invariance as sigma_n o tau_pi = sigma_n for the permutation automorphisms tau_pi (pr_i o tau_pi = pr_{pi(i)}), together with the invariance beta_pi(tau_pi^*F_j) = F_j. The one imported step (elementary null, no uses) is split into six steps: coefficients and sections, T_0,T_1 without common zero on P^1 (Stacks 01NG), the fibre computation with kappa[t] a domain, the morphism (Stacks 01NE/01NF), the permutation isomorphism beta_pi, and the comparison of the two projections. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-product-linear-forms-coefficients (Mathlib leaf, Finset.prod_add) and lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor (unsplit; pullback/tensor/fibres of invertible modules, Stacks 01CD, 0B8L, 0B8K, 0098, 01CB). stmt_deps: added the projective-space, fibre-product, twisting-sheaf, invertible-module, functor-of-points and phi nodes; def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism kept.
